cards.text: Psalm 120 starts with a label: 'A song of ascents.' The psalmist is looking back on a time of real distress. And in that distress, the psalmist made the smartest move there is: crying out to the LORD.

cards.question: In distress, the psalmist cried out to the LORD. Fill it in: 'In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He ___ me.'

cards.text: He ANSWERED, friend. No hold music, no pressing 9 forty times, no robot voice saying 'Your call is VERY important to us.' So now the psalmist prays, 'Deliver my soul, O LORD.'

cards.question: The psalmist prays, 'Deliver my soul, O LORD,' and names the trouble. Deliver from what?

answers.text: Lying lips and a deceitful tongue
A strong enemy and a mighty army
Hunger and a dry and weary land

cards.question: Next, the psalmist stops praying to the LORD and asks someone, 'What will He do to you, and what will be added to you…' Who is the psalmist talking to now?

cards.text: That tongue's been running its mouth this whole time, and NOW it's the one in the hot seat. The very next line brings in a warrior.

cards.question: Right after the question to the deceitful tongue, a warrior shows up. What comes from the warrior?
The psalmist asks the deceitful tongue what will be done to it, and the next line brings sharp arrows and burning coals of the broom tree. What is that picture about?

answers.text: What is coming to the deceitful tongue
How the psalmist will win a battle
Why the psalmist had to leave home

cards.text: Then the psalmist names the neighborhood: Meshech, and the tents of Kedar. Way back, Meshech was a son of Japheth, and Kedar was a son of Ishmael (Gen 10:2; 25:13).

cards.question: The psalmist is happy to be living in Meshech and among the tents of Kedar.

cards.text: Nope. The psalmist says, 'Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar!' I know that feeling, friend: years in a junk drawer, wedged under the takeout menus, going, how did I end up HERE?

cards.question: It's not just where the psalmist lives. It's who. What does the psalmist say about the people there?
The psalmist says living among people who hate peace has only gone on for a short while.

cards.text: Last line of the song, friend. The psalmist tells you where they stand, and what happens every single time they open their mouth in that neighborhood. Let's just say nobody's passing around the cookie box.

cards.question: The psalmist's last line. Fill it in: 'I am in favor of ___; but when I speak, they want ___.'
